title: Standardized Intermittent Shoreline Boat Electrofishing for Rivers in Sweden
author: Näslund, Staveley, et al.
materials: education in ethics for animal research

steps.title: Define site and transect
steps.instruction: Outline a transect through the chosen site along one or both river shorelines. Divide the transect into sections of fixed length (optional but recommended). Insert unfished separation distances between sections (optional but recommended) to extend the overall fished stretch.

steps.title: Set electrofishing unit parameters
steps.instruction: Install anodes on adjustable booms if available, spacing them 2 m apart to obtain an effective fished width of 4 m. Adjust the electrofishing unit in the water before starting so that the attraction distance from each anode is 1 m. If anode spacing is fixed, determine the effective fished width on‑site.

steps.title: Follow timing and safety guidelines
steps.instruction: Plan to fish only during daylight hours (avoid dusk, dawn, and night). Schedule sampling for late summer or autumn (late July to early October) to include young‑of‑the‑year fish.

steps.title: Position boat near shoreline
steps.instruction: Drive the boat as close to the shoreline as possible, navigating through vegetation and around obstacles (e.g., overhanging trees, fallen logs, stones, jetties) while maintaining the systematic sequence.

steps.title: Perform intermittent electrofishing
steps.instruction: Conduct intermittent electrofishing in each section using a repeat cycle of shock and movement.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the power for exactly 5 seconds.
Move the boat downstream one boat length if the current is slow, or two boat lengths if the current is faster, allowing netting personnel to empty nets and the driver to record notes.
Repeat the 5‑second shock and movement cycle until the entire section has been sampled.

steps.title: Record effective fished width
steps.instruction: Log the effective fished width for the operation (e.g., 4 m when anodes are spaced 2 m apart) in the field notebook.
